Arrival checks for companion animals

When you reach the desk, we keep the handoff calm and simple. I look over the booking, confirm the traveler is in the right place, and make sure the carrier or enclosure is ready for the next step. The goal is to keep the animal settled and the owner informed without adding extra stress.

For small dog travel, <<FACT F068>> I also check that the carrier is clean, secure, and easy to carry through the terminal. If anything looks loose or out of place, I pause the process and ask for a quick correction before the animal moves on.

Birds need a little extra care at arrival. <<FACT F083>> I ask the traveler to keep the carrier level, avoid sudden movements, and stay close until the handoff is complete. Calm handling helps the bird stay steady while we update the desk ledger and pass along the next instructions.

Reptile arrivals follow the same careful rhythm, but the prep can be different. <<FACT F060>> I review the setup with the traveler, confirm the enclosure is closed properly, and make sure the animal stays away from heat, drafts, and rough handling while on the move.

If a carrier label is faded, a latch seems weak, or the animal seems uneasy, tell the desk team right away. The ground team will move the carrier carefully between services, and we note service changes in the ledger so nothing gets missed. That way, everyone stays on the same page and the trip keeps moving smoothly.

If you need extra help, the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways is ready to guide you at the counter.
